newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares fall in thin trade; Elite soars.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares fall in thin trade; Elite soars.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower across the board in thin trade on Sunday as investors remained indifferent to a cabinet discussion on capital market reform, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 1.37 percent, or 2.49 points, to 179.19 on low turnover of 52 million shekels against 54 million on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index lost 1.38 percent to 188.41.
"On a normal day we would have seen reaction to the meeting but now the market is dead and investors are losing interest," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.

The Israeli cabinet will reconvene on Sunday evening to discuss a package of reform measures for the capital market. The measures recommended by a panel headed by Treasury Director General David Brodett are aimed at encouraging long-term savings over short-term alternatives.
The most controversial measure is a tax on short- and medium-term savings.
"Nothing will come of the (Brodett) report and the government will not adopt the recommendations. Everything looks gloomy and the market has no future," Scharia said.

Elite Industries, the second-most active share, surged 4.25 percent to 1,255 on volume of 2.7 million shekels. Elite said it will enter into negotiations with a European food company for the sale of its three coffee roasting factories in Spain, Belgium and France.

Clal Electronics Industries fell 3.5 percent to 23,730 after its sudsidiary Scitex said on Friday it will post a third-quarter operating loss greater than the $11 million it reported in the second quarter.
"Trading was very dull today and the market was sleepy. If the Brodett recommendations are not accepted the market will fall sharply," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
"Approval of the recommendations will leave the market at the current level," he said.
The most active share was Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 2.5 percent to 135,396 on volume of 4.0 million shekels.
Koor Industries lost 1.5 percent to 26,603 on volume of 3.5 million shekels.
